title: TS-25 Policy kernel B with durable approvals
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 25 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 25); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Port authorization ceiling, approval binding, authorized connections and overnight-gated logic, and make the state durable. Python kept it in memory; here it is Messaging items APPROVAL#, RULE#, CONN#.

## Kind
mechanical-port: the Python source below is the specification. Keep its structure, names (camelCase), branches and messages. Do not redesign anything.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/25-policy-kernel-b-with-durable-approvals origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): policy kernel B with durable approvals

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/25-policy-kernel-b-with-durable-approvals
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

- `conversation/src/policy/approval-binding.ts`
- `conversation/src/policy/connections.ts`

- `conversation/src/store/codecs/approval.ts`

- `conversation/features-support/steps/approval.steps.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
Item keys: pk `{t}#approvals` sk `APPROVAL#<id>`; pk `{t}#rules` sk `RULE#<id>`; pk `{t}#connections` sk `CONN#<id>`. Each codec has `encode`/`decode` as in ticket 2. The in-memory dicts of Python's ControlPlane named in port-map section 0 (`_approval_binding`, `_auto_review_rules`, `_authorized_connections`) are replaced by store reads and conditional writes.

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)

Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Stop rules
